source.title: Forking: Sudden Overfitting Under Replay
source.authors: Shan-Bin Yu; Shao-Yang Guo; Hao-Ran Zhao; Dan-Ni Yu; Zi-Ming Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full 42-page paper; no truncation or garbling is evident.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports controlled results showing that replay and an over-encoding memory pathway can produce a large train–validation gap, refining the scope of generalization claims. Its tested replay conditions do not match the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on replay-induced train–validation divergence in language models with n-gram memory. Cited prior-work results are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter-selection screens in Appendix C.2 are not rows because they select settings rather than report a separate test of a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study tests replay-induced overfitting in language models with n-gram memory, which none of V1–V8 names. It does not compare random versus natural labels, network widths, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of examples selected by memorization influence. Masking memory retrieval retains training examples and therefore does not test V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly accurate, but freezing does not uniformly reduce the gap: freezing at step 338 increases the step-1000 gap relative to control. The authors conclude that n-gram over-encoding amplifies replay-induced divergence, with incomplete continuation coverage and replay-driven sharpening contributing especially in rare contexts. Low-frequency masking mitigates divergence, and freezing reduces gaps in the continued-pretraining experiments without eliminating them. The post-training evidence uses all-token continued pretraining and a static RLVR-like proxy, rather than response-only SFT or on-policy reinforcement learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses language-model training on replayed natural text with learned n-gram memory and measures cross-entropy train–validation gaps; the listed versions concern label memorization, width, image architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures or example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Gap changes with n-gram injection route, table capacity, corpus size, replay duration, frequency masking threshold, hash reseeding, table freezing, and training source. In the DeepSeek-style experiment, low-frequency mask threshold changes the gap.

fits_no_version.finding: N-gram memory amplifies replay-associated train–validation divergence in NanoGPT; disabling higher-order pathways improves final validation BPB from 1.6769 to 1.0768. A DeepSeek-style full-memory model also develops a 3.316-nat gap, without a completed no-gram comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-indexed n-gram memory can amplify replay-induced overfitting in language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger corpora reduce the measured gap, while extended replay produces substantially larger gaps in memory-equipped models than in the no-gram control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replay-induced overfitting depends on corpus size, repetition count, and memory architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-frequency retrieval masking reduces gaps and improves validation loss in tested configurations; repeated hash reseeding suppresses gap accumulation. High-frequency masking has much less effect on the gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rare-context retrieval and stable context-to-row assignments contribute to replay-induced overfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing tables after the first pass does not prevent divergence and increases the step-1000 gap in one comparison. Freezing from the start of continued pretraining reduces endpoint gaps across four sources, but leaves residual gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Freezing n-gram tables does not prevent replay-induced overfitting; its effect depends on training history and intervention timing.

record.problems: The main controlled experiments use a single shard and mostly seed 42. DeepSeek-style no-gram controls failed with non-finite training loss, so that architecture lacks a completed no-gram comparison. Several comparisons use online training loss from the current batch and fixed held-out batches. The text notes nondeterministic trajectories, and some individual-context trajectories reverse between reruns. The continued-training seed spread is reported as small, but broader production-scale effects remain untested.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted individual continuation-token probability plots and additional context-frequency decompositions because they are context-specific diagnostics rather than separately reported overall train–validation gap conditions for the versions. Figure-only table-capacity trend is not assigned numeric values because the text gives no exact points.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level generalization under random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and local-connectivity or initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing high-memorization examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not whether the reported replay effects occurred. Citations to Zhang et al. and Feldman–Zhang provide background rather than tests of V1 or V8. No omitted result bearing on a listed version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization; the named image architectures, datasets and training recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effects of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons under the stated tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and the listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size, augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing test accuracy with random-example removal.

rows.subject: NanoGPT with both bigram and trigram tables (input route)
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden dimension 768; 6 attention heads; vocabulary 8192; sequence length 2048
rows.operation_detail: Train on a fixed single-shard corpus with replay for 1000 updates; report online train–validation gap.
rows.measure: Online gap, validation loss minus current-batch training loss
rows.note: The text describes the gap widening in a staircase aligned with replay boundaries; no exact step-1000 value is stated here.
rows.check: The measured gap does not establish any listed version. Appendix D supplies a step-1000 control gap of 2.724 nats; Figure 4 itself describes a 2000-update trajectory.

source_check.correct: The both-table input-injection control has a step-1000 raw online gap of 2.724 nats. Figure 4 describes 2000 updates.
source_check.problem: The step-1000 value is available in Appendix D, although not stated numerically beside Figure 4.

relation.reason: Related work discusses random-label fitting, dropout, and memorization of rare examples, but the study neither tests the listed versions nor uses their findings as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: Replay-induced language-model overfitting, retrieval masking, and table freezing test none of V1–V8. Retrieval masking retains training examples and their loss terms, so it does not test V8.

source_check.notes: The DeepSeek-style model lacks a completed matched no-gram control. Freezing increases the minimal-setting step-1000 gap but reduces continued-pretraining endpoint gaps; these are different interventions and settings.
